references.text: The laws about compensation when someone falls into an open pit concern responsibility for others' safety, the same principle as building a railing on a roof.
The responsibility to care for other people's property and lives reflects the same concern for one's neighbor as building a railing.
The prohibition against standing passively when your neighbor's life is in danger supports the duty to prevent accidents.
The command to love your neighbor as yourself is the foundation for protecting others from harm.
The watchman's responsibility to warn of danger corresponds to the housebuilder's responsibility to protect people.
God demands accountability for human blood, which underscores the seriousness of preventing fatal accidents.
Avoiding innocent blood being shed in the land is a recurring theme linked to safety measures.
Jesus quotes the command to love your neighbor, which is the underlying principle for protecting others from harm.
